features.lev_equivalent: N/A (Lev is TS monorepo, Rust components emerging)
features.notes: Full platform distributed as a single Rust binary. Docker or bare. No Kubernetes required.

features.name: Unified AI platform and single-pane operations
features.lev_equivalent: Lev has workstreams, FlowMind, dashboards, and event state, but no unified deploy/run/serve platform surface.
features.notes: Keep Lev's local-first source of truth; use Union as product-surface benchmark.

features.name: Pure-Python async workflow authoring
features.lev_equivalent: FlowMind graphs and Lev commands are declarative/CLI-first; Python-style task authoring is not a core ergonomic.
features.notes: Useful as an authoring benchmark, not as a reason to replace FlowMind.

features.name: TaskEnvironment shared infrastructure contract
features.lev_equivalent: Lev has runtime surfaces and skill/workstream state, but no first-class reusable task environment abstraction.
features.notes: Likely high-value extraction for tool/runtime adapters.

features.name: Task-level CPU, memory, GPU, disk, and accelerator resources
features.lev_equivalent: Lev has budget and execution-policy concepts, but not typed per-task compute resources across substrates.
features.notes: Separate generic resource hints from ML/GPU-specific extensions.

features.name: Files, directories, DataFrames, and artifact movement
features.lev_equivalent: Lev tracks artifacts and events, but lacks a complete typed large-artifact transport contract.
features.notes: Presigned/reference semantics map better than copying payloads into core state.

features.name: Fanout and dynamic parallel execution
features.lev_equivalent: Lev has subagent and loop parallelism, but no typed user-workload fanout primitive.
features.notes: Keep agent coordination and workload fanout as separate contracts.

features.name: Secrets declaration and runtime injection
features.lev_equivalent: AgentGuard and local policy exist, but secret lease/injection is not uniformly modeled for deployable workloads.
features.notes: Must be guarded by scoped leases and audit receipts before promotion.

features.name: Triggers, schedules, and webhooks
features.lev_equivalent: Codex app automations and Lev loops exist, but workflow trigger semantics are split across tools.
features.notes: Unify with existing automation semantics instead of adding a parallel scheduler.

features.name: Task result caching
features.lev_equivalent: Lev has memoization-like state and trace artifacts in places, but no uniform task-output cache contract.
features.notes: Cache identity must include code, inputs, environment, and policy.

features.name: Function-level traces and checkpoint visibility
features.lev_equivalent: Lev has trace/event concepts, but no standardized function-level workload trace decorator.
features.notes: Map to existing event spans before introducing decorator-style APIs.

features.name: HTML reports from runs
features.lev_equivalent: Lev can generate reports/dashboards, but run-scoped report artifacts are not a uniform contract.
features.notes: Good fit for existing `now` and dashboard artifact paths.

features.name: Local, devbox, and remote run modes
features.lev_equivalent: Lev spans local shells, tmux, automations, and agents, but not a single run-mode matrix for workloads.
features.notes: This is a clean model for local/remote capability negotiation.

features.name: Agentic AI workflow patterns
features.lev_equivalent: Lev has rich agent workflows, but less deployable-agent-as-workload packaging.
features.notes: Keep Lev's agent lifecycle authority; borrow packaging and service boundaries.

features.name: Sandboxed agent workload execution
features.lev_equivalent: AgentGuard and dcg guardrails exist, but workload sandboxing is not expressed as deployable task environments.
features.notes: Bridge policy authority before runtime packaging.

features.name: RBAC, audit, tenant isolation, and presigned data access
features.lev_equivalent: Lev has local trust boundaries and AgentGuard direction, but not enterprise RBAC/audit across deployable data planes.
features.notes: High-value architecture reference for remote/federated Lev.

features.name: External data and compute integrations
features.lev_equivalent: Lev supports tool/plugin expansion, but not a typed connector registry for workload execution.
features.notes: Use as registry-shape reference, not as a dependency list.

features.name: Run/serve/deploy/build/log/abort CLI verbs
features.lev_equivalent: Lev has many CLI surfaces; lifecycle verbs are not normalized for workloads.
features.notes: Align with the repo's poly naming contract before adding aliases.

features.name: Example repository with cloud/local/preview validation modes
features.lev_equivalent: Lev has scattered examples/tests, but no canonical external-reference example harness.
features.notes: Useful immediately for how Lev should validate example-heavy docs.

features.name: Helm, Terraform, operator, and EKS blueprint deployment automation
features.lev_equivalent: Lev has local setup and automation patterns, but no cloud deployment stack.
features.notes: Reference only until Lev has a concrete deployable control-plane target.

features.name: Control plane / data plane split
features.lev_equivalent: Lev architecture already separates FlowMind control, orchestration execution, graph state, and Event Bus, but lacks a managed/federated data-plane implementation.
features.notes: Strong architectural reference for preserving Lev state authority across remote substrates.

features.name: Failure recovery, retries, versioning, and reproducibility
features.lev_equivalent: Lev has handoffs, Event Bus concepts, and workstream state, but workload retry/version contracts are not unified.
features.notes: Translate into contract tests before implementation.

features.name: Projects, domains, users, and organization management
features.lev_equivalent: Lev has workstreams and plugins, but not enterprise org/project administration.
features.notes: Useful only if Lev grows multi-tenant platform mode.

features.name: Reusable warm containers and Actors
features.lev_equivalent: Lev starts processes/agents but lacks a workload-level warm container or actor reuse primitive.
features.notes: High-value if Lev adds long-running tool/service pools.

features.name: Cloud image building
features.lev_equivalent: Lev does not build/push workload container images as a platform primitive.
features.notes: Do not implement before a deployable runtime target exists.

features.name: First-class FastAPI, Streamlit, webhook, and app serving
features.lev_equivalent: Lev can generate UI/report artifacts, but does not run user apps as first-class workload deployments.
features.notes: Promote only behind explicit local-server/remote-server contracts.

features.name: vLLM/SGLang LLM serving with OpenAI-compatible API
features.lev_equivalent: Lev calls external models and tools, but does not deploy model-serving infrastructure.
features.notes: Reference for provider symmetry, not a near-term core feature.

features.name: App autoscaling and scale-to-zero
features.lev_equivalent: Lev has automations and processes, but no autoscaled app workload plane.
features.notes: Requires service runtime and observability before it matters.

features.name: Model prefetching and sharding
features.lev_equivalent: Lev has no model artifact staging or GPU sharding workflow.
features.notes: Useful only if Lev becomes a model host, not just a model client.

features.name: Cost observability and resource dashboards
features.lev_equivalent: Lev tracks budgets in process/policy contexts but lacks a consolidated cost dashboard for workload runs.
features.notes: Valuable for agent/runtime cost accounting even without GPU workloads.

features.name: Outbound-only zero-trust data-plane tunnel
features.lev_equivalent: Lev has no remote data-plane tunnel product yet.
features.notes: High-value future remote-worker pattern.

features.name: Notebook and Jupyter workflow authoring
features.lev_equivalent: Lev does not provide notebook-native workflow authoring.
features.notes: Not core unless user workflows move into notebook environments.

features.name: Production case studies and scale claims
features.lev_equivalent: Lev should use these as benchmark inspiration only.
features.notes: Do not treat marketing claims as implementation requirements without reproducing tests.

features.name: Flyte 1 service decomposition
features.lev_equivalent: Lev should not recreate Flyte 1 services, but the split remains useful historical architecture evidence.
features.notes: Prefer current Flyte 2 SDK/core evidence for new design.

features.name: Scene-configured world DSL for entities, actions, consequences, auto-tick, perception, and narrator
features.notes: One YAML scene defines the playable world and its runtime rules.

features.name: Flat entity state with numeric constraint enforcement and reusable templates
features.notes: WorldSeed stores world truth as flat entity properties plus clamped numeric constraints.

features.name: Agent registry with character/world-state split, omniscient/system flags, and think intervals
features.notes: Character cards are kept separate from world-state fields and runtime wake policy.

features.name: Background tick runner with interval, max-tick, timeout, and DM budget controls
features.notes: The runtime loop is first-class and bounded.

features.name: Action queue with one-action-per-agent-per-tick semantics
features.notes: Agent actions are queued and drained at the next tick with turn-like pacing.

features.name: Deterministic precondition/effect DSL for predictable outcomes
features.notes: Predictable actions resolve without an LLM through a declarative rule/effect layer.

features.name: Multi-pass consequence scanner with stable re-scan until no new triggers fire
features.notes: Consequence rules are rescanned until the world reaches a local fixpoint.

features.name: Structured DM arbitration with allowlisted ops, retry, rollback, and token accounting
features.notes: Ambiguous actions resolve through a bounded DM that returns validated structured effects.

features.name: Per-agent perception filters with visibility rules, event scopes, and hidden properties
features.notes: Agents never see raw world truth; they get scoped snapshots.

features.name: Inbox plus wake policy with push events, whispers, and think intervals
features.notes: Wake behavior is separate from the action loop and supports urgency.

features.name: Append-only run recorder with latest state, per-tick snapshots, transient resume, and summaries
features.notes: Runs are inspectable and partially replayable from persisted artifacts.

features.name: Lobby/start/resume/step/pause/stop lifecycle API for a live world
features.lev_equivalent: daemon/dashboard surfaces without a world-runtime contract
features.notes: Operator control over world execution is explicit and tested.

features.name: Live operator dashboard with map, event stream, highlights, data inspector, and scene lobby
features.notes: WorldSeed includes a real operator UX, not just a CLI.

features.name: GM queued mutations and natural-language resolve commands
features.notes: Operator changes can be staged then applied at the next tick boundary.

features.name: OpenClaw gateway plugin with SOUL/WORLD/SKILL injection and per-agent sessions
features.lev_equivalent: no shipped OpenClaw bridge in canon
features.notes: WorldSeed's bridge is concrete and operator-friendly, but shell-specific.

features.name: Narrator / observer system agent with chapter publishing and whisper options

features.name: Scene portability by swapping only YAML while keeping one runtime
features.notes: Same engine, different worlds, different stories.

features.name: Broad test matrix across unit, integration, e2e, browser, scenario, and stress suites
features.lev_equivalent: broader repo testing without comparable world-runtime coverage
features.notes: WorldSeed tests the runtime as a product, not only as a library.

features.name: Blackboard shared working memory with provenance and subscriptions
features.notes: Lev already ships a more reusable version of this than WorldSeed's implicit state coordination.

features.name: Behavior-tree, GOAP, HTN, and director primitives separated from the world loop
features.notes: Lev already exposes reusable decision primitives that WorldSeed does not package as first-class modules.

features.name: Predictive world-model lane explicitly separated from admission and projection
features.notes: Lev now has the right architecture slot, but not the runtime.

features.name: Provider-neutral runtime surfaces and registry-first tool exposure beyond one agent shell
features.notes: Lev is stronger on surface architecture, but not yet for a world runtime.
